items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: If you get to work with Raymond Burke and get to know how he plays, you know that he is really outstanding

ctx.x: music had its place where they had the marching bands, which was a definite, a particular style of New Orleans, which I think belonged entirely, mostly, to the to the to the colored people. However, I do believe this, that the white musicians brought jazz to a higher level, to a higher standard, in when they brought it to New York. For instance, Nick LaRocca always said this, that that when they went to New York with their band, they played a different type of jazz. In fact, if you listen to it, if you listen to…

I think you have a good point, because look, for example, at the reputation, commercially speaking of George Lewis and Raymond Burke. Raymond in his own way is, seems to me, is fully great a jazz musician as George is.
Well, I think every bit, every bit, I would even go so far as to say that I think even greater in some respects.
